Boundary powers and angular Fourier spectra

Reconstructed and self-checked by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), Ultra reasoning effort, October 2026. Earlier edition: GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI), Ultra reasoning effort. Original exposition: CC0. Supplied programme foundations retain their stated licences.

Parabolic boundary powers have spectra in a half-plane. Continuing their exponent through zero turns an ordinary density into derivatives of a point mass. Circular complex poles and trace-free spherical principal values instead have regular angular transforms. In each case the defining limit fixes the distribution at the singular set before its Fourier transform is computed.

Pairings are complex bilinear and , where . The supplied Fourier foundation, F1–F5, proves the Schwartz topology, compact-test density, Gaussian constant, inversion and all coordinate rules. The scalar foundation, §§12 and 13.1–13.5, 13.7–13.10, and integration foundation, §§15.0–15.1, 15.6 and 16, supply calculus, bumps, convergence, Fubini and changes of variables. The Gamma foundation, G0–G2 and W4a–W4e, supplies the entire reciprocal , its product, zeros and their exact derivatives.

We use the exact earlier proofs in U048, Theorem 1.1 for tempered tensors; U053, Lemma 1.1 and Theorem 2.1 for complex Laplace integration and the full Cauchy transform; U029, Theorem 2.1 for circular cutoffs and their derivative normalization; and U034, Theorem 4.1, with the Newton Hessian proved in U028, Solution 8, for spherical principal values. The full Coulomb transform is U051, Theorem 1.1. Measurable polar integration is proved in the angular foundation, A4; the latitude area calculation is U035, Theorem 1.1, first proof paragraph. No external citation replaces these programme proofs.

Write . A bounded Schwartz set has a common bound for each . Strong convergence below means uniform convergence of pairings on every such set. Fixed differentiation, polynomial multiplication and invertible linear changes preserve bounded Schwartz sets, by their finite product and chain rules; their transposes therefore preserve strong convergence.

Circular Cauchy poles have regular angular spectra

The circular prescription is U029, Theorem 2.1, proves the exact order , existence and dilation/rotation normalization, and

Theorem 2.1. This normalized distribution is tempered and as a whole regular distribution.

Proof. The source is locally integrable and tempered, and (2.1) therefore defines a tempered extension. It agrees with the original cutoff on Schwartz tests as well. For , subtract near zero a radial compact cutoff times the degree- Taylor polynomial. Every subtracted monomial has angular frequency of magnitude at most ; after multiplication by its angular integral is zero. The remainder is with a fixed derivative bound, so times it is absolutely integrable in two dimensions. The unchanged tail is controlled by a Schwartz weight. At the kernel itself is locally integrable. These are the actual cutoff limits, and uniqueness on Schwartz space follows also from compact-test density.

U053 proves on the whole plane. The multiplier of is , so (2.1) gives Its coefficient simplifies to that in (2.2). The absolute value is , which is locally integrable also at and has polynomial growth. Polynomial multiplication therefore preserves the whole regular distribution, including its normalization at the origin.
